evidence.text: Single-column deviations at most +/-13.6%. Perfect balance would need Column 2/12: 171 steps and Column 7: 834 steps, about an 8-hour game. Optimal +-1-step board [3,5,8,10,12,14,12,10,8,5,3] cuts deviation to +/-3.09%, 4x better with +1 step.

Best balance under 20 steps: [4,7,11,14,17,20,17,14,11,7,4], +/-2.17%, 6x improvement. Best linear step=2.25 keeps [3,5,8,10,12,14,...] at +/-3.09%; integer step base=5 step=4 gives +/-3.32%. Multi-column reality: Column 7 in {6,7,8} finishes in ~2 turns vs Column 2 in {2,3,12} in ~30 turns.

nodes.text: Advice: play 50% rule on columns 5-9; designers prioritize playability plus handicaps.

evidence.text: Conclusion: four-dice flattens distribution (P7 64.4% vs P2 13.2%, 4.88x vs 6x); combos matter ({6,7,8} 92% vs {2,3,12} 44%); probabilistic strategies dominate; consistency beats speed; P1 advantage 55.59%; forced-move rule compensates imbalance; perfect balance unnecessary.

For players: use FiftyPercentSurvival, aim for columns 5-9, avoid columns 2-3 and 11-12, prioritize consistency. For designers: prioritize playability over perfection, consider handicaps. Open question: can any strategy break 75%, or is ~70% the limit?
